mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth over the last quarter suggests strengthening economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 1% in the last two months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a weakening economy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in the last two months, it indicates a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending is expected to rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it indicates inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) both increase by more than 1% in the last quarter, it signals a broad-based strengthening of economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both increase > 1% in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
